section_overviews.commercial_observer:
Zara Doubles Footprint at a Macerich Shopping Center in Los Angeles County: Fashion firm Zara is more than doubling its footprint at a Southern California shopping center. The clothing retailer is expanding from 22,000 square feet to a 45,000-square-foot flagship opening next year at Macerich ’s 1.3 million-square-foot Los Cerritos Center in southeast Los Angeles County.

Happier Grocery to Open Second NYC Location on the Upper East Side: A healthy grocery retailer is opening its second New York City location on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. Happier Grocery has signed a 20,500-square-foot lease at CSC Real Estate ’s 210 East 86th Street , where it plans to open a health food store like its original one on Canal Street in the second half of 2027,.

Sephora’s Meatpacking District Store Relocates to 401 West 14th Street: Beauty retailer Sephora is taking a walk up the block to 401 West 14th Street . The makeup giant has signed a 4,200-square-foot deal with landlords Taconic Partners and Nuveen Real Estate to relocate its Meatpacking District store one block north from 21-27 Ninth Avenue , according to the landlords.

Legion Investment Group, SMA Equities Pair on 300K-SF UES Resi Project: Legion Investment Group and SMA Equities have teamed on a 300,000-square-foot residential development rising on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. The new partnership secured a $99 million pre-development loan for the 37-story project at 1491-1497 Third Avenue on Thursday, according to The Real Deal , which first reported.

Retail Demand Grows as Construction Hits Record Low: US retailers posted a net gain of 127 stores through Aug. 28, adding 28.6M SF of occupied retail space.

Invesco REIT Buys Raleigh Retail Center for $87.2M: Invesco REIT acquired Knightdale Marketplace for $87.2M, including closing and leasing costs, according to AltsWire. The 323,113 SF shopping center is 100% leased with a weighted average lease term of about seven years.

Core Retail Sales Hit Record as In-Store Spending Rises: Core retail sales rose 1.2% in August and 5.6% year over year, with gains across nine of 10 major retail categories. Store-based sales increased 0.6%, outpacing headline inflation and marking the second-largest monthly gain in the past 14 months.

Mall Values Jump 13% as Retail Recovery Accelerates: Green Street says mall values increased 13% over the past year, the strongest gain among 10 commercial property sectors. Limited new supply, resilient consumer spending and tenant upgrades have supported occupancy, rent growth and investor interest.

items.headline: Zara Doubles Footprint at a Macerich Shopping Center in Los Angeles County

The clothing retailer is expanding from 22,000 square feet to a 45,000-square-foot flagship opening next year at Macerich ’s 1.3 million-square-foot Los Cerritos Center in southeast Los Angeles County. Zara’s existing store will remain open during construction. The property is at 239 Los Cerritos Center near the border between L.A. and Orange counties.…

items.headline: Retail Demand Grows as Construction Hits Record Low
items.summary: US retailers posted a net gain of 127 stores through Aug. 28, adding 28.6M SF of occupied retail space. Retail recorded 10.2M SF of positive Q2 net absorption while vacancy remained near 4.4%. Q2 completions fell to a record-low 5.2M SF as construction costs continued to outpace rent growth across most markets. Key Takeaways Bisnow reports that US retail leasing and store growth are accelerating while new construction remains constrained. Coresight Research counted a net gain of 127 store openings through Aug.…

items.headline: Invesco REIT Buys Raleigh Retail Center for $87.2M
items.summary: Invesco REIT acquired Knightdale Marketplace for $87.2M, including closing and leasing costs, according to AltsWire. The 323,113 SF shopping center is 100% leased with a weighted average lease term of about seven years. The REIT raised $79.2M quarter to date through August, nearly double the $46.2M reported through July. Key Takeaways AltsWire reports that Invesco Real Estate Income Trust bought the Raleigh-area retail center for $87.2M.…

items.headline: Core Retail Sales Hit Record as In-Store Spending Rises
items.summary: Core retail sales rose 1.2% in August and 5.6% year over year, with gains across nine of 10 major retail categories. Store-based sales increased 0.6%, outpacing headline inflation and marking the second-largest monthly gain in the past 14 months. Preliminary Q3 2026 data showed positive net absorption across single- and multi-tenant retail, with supply roughly in line with demand. Key Takeaways Consumer spending strengthened broadly in August, supporting both online and physical retail.…

items.headline: Mall Values Jump 13% as Retail Recovery Accelerates
items.summary: Green Street says mall values increased 13% over the past year, the strongest gain among 10 commercial property sectors. Limited new supply, resilient consumer spending and tenant upgrades have supported occupancy, rent growth and investor interest. Major owners including URW and CBL are increasing exposure again, although mall values remain below their decade-ago peak. Key Takeaways The Wall Street Journal reports that malls have become the top-performing commercial real estate sector after years of distress.…

items.headline: Restaurant Traffic Falls 2.4% Across US in August
items.summary: US dining visits fell 2.4% year over year in August, reversing gradual improvement recorded in June and July. Overall retail visits still rose 0.3%, but growth slowed sharply from 1.7% in July. September traffic will help show how much of August’s restaurant weakness came from calendar timing versus softer demand. Key Takeaways GlobeSt reports that US dining visits fell broadly in August while retail traffic remained slightly positive .…

items.headline: Construction Firm Brasfield & Gorrie Inks 19K-SF Lease in Broward County
items.summary: Construction firm Brasfield & Gorrie is relocating in South Florida, from Coral Gables to Weston, where it signed a 19,330-square-foot lease. The general contractor will move into the Weston Pointe I building in the second quarter of 2027, according to JLL , which represented the tenant. It will occupy most of the third floor within the four-story building at 2400 North Commerce Parkway , just west of I-75. It’s part of the two-building Weston Pointe campus that was built between 1999 and 2001.…

items.headline: Pistola Denim Takes Nearly 18K SF at ROW DTLA
items.summary: Denim and womenswear company Pistola Denim has signed a 17,922-square-foot office lease at Atlas Capital Group ’s ROW DTLA , adding another fashion company to the nearly 2 million-square-foot Downtown Los Angeles complex. Grace Na founded Pistola in 2013. The L.A.-based brand will move its creative team from warehouse and distribution space in Vernon. The terms of the lease were not disclosed.…

items.headline: Cerity Partners Expands to 68K SF at Global Holdings’ 99 Park Avenue
items.summary: Wealth management firm Cerity Partners is expanding its offices at Midtown’s 99 Park Avenue . The tenant, which just expanded to 48,671 square feet at the building in December , has signed a deal for 19,600 additional square feet on the eighth floor of Global Holdings ’ 26-story office building, bringing its total footprint to about 68,300 square feet, according to the landlord. It was a 15-year deal with an asking rent starting at $90 per square foot, Global Holdings confirmed.…

items.headline: Toys R Us Plans 120 Holiday Stores in Retail Push
items.summary: Toys R Us plans 120 temporary standalone stores for the holiday season, compared with 36 permanent US locations. The pop-ups expand a 2023 strategy that used 24 temporary stores, while the brand also adds airport and shop-in-shop formats. National retail vacancy was 4.2% at the end of June, with limited new construction keeping available space relatively tight. Key Takeaways Toys R Us is preparing a major temporary store expansion for the holiday season.…

items.headline: Asian-American Deli Café Hestia Signs 8K-SF Lease at 570 Lexington Avenue
items.summary: A cafe serving Asian and American cuisine is opening a fourth Manhattan location, Commercial Observer has learned. Café Hestia , a group of family-run delis, has signed a 20-year, 8,000-square-foot lease at the base of the Feil Organization ’s 570 Lexington Avenue , which it will likely also use as a catering facility, according to tenant broker Kassin Sabbagh Realty (KSR).…

items.headline: Stroller Brand Uppababy Relocates Store to 156 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights
items.summary: Known for its distinctive strollers, baby gear brand Uppababy is relocating its store within Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. The high-end baby accessories brand is opening a 3,780-square-foot brick-and-mortar location at Owen Realty ’s 156 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights, according to broker JLL . Uppababy will move next year from 90 Smith Street in Cobble Hill, where it established its Brooklyn retail and service “hub” in about 2019.…

items.summary: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani wants to get the city into the subsidized grocery business. Plus, a pair of new lawsuits could stop the scheme faster than you can cancel an Instacart order, and many critics decry the initiative as the first step in a descent into socialism.…

items.headline: Billion-Dollar Blockbusters Won’t Revive L.A.’s Film Industry
items.summary: Hollywood, or at least some aspect of it, had a summer. Between massive box office performances from “The Odyssey” (partially shot in Los Angeles), “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “Obsession,” the industry appears to have recaptured some of its cultural magnetism and moneymaking ways. Adjusted for inflation, the movie industry’s $4.76 billion summer ticket haul represented a 26 percent jump from the summer of 2025.…
